newsitem.title: USA: Take a cruise without going overboard.
newsitem.headline: Take a cruise without going overboard.

text.p: There are two feet of snow in Cleveland, New York is expecting flurries and the sun has said goodbye to Boston. Winter has pushed aside autumn with a vengeance.
What better time to start thinking about a warm weather vacation -- a cruise.
Cruises have become vacation opportunities for travelers on a budget, as well as for luxury travelers.

Currently, only about 7 percent of the U.S. public takes cruises. However, between 1995 and 1998, the capacity of the top four lines is expected to increase by an average of 70 percent, said Larry Fishkin, founder and president of The Cruise Line Inc., a Miami-based cruise discounter.
This could spell bargains for vacationers, as cruise companies look for novel ways to fill their ships.

Cruises are all-inclusive vacations, offering room, board, entertainment, child care and other extras. Some cruise packages also include transportation to and from the port of embarkation. This allows the budget conscious to plan ahead.
When selecting a cruise, keep a sharp eye on the price, which may change by the time you finally set sail.

"It is not unusual in this market that prices drop after you book," Fishkin said. "You need to tell the travel agent to check at the time of final payment (typically 60 days ahead) so that they are sure of getting the best prossible price.
"Prices change. It's a reality in this market."

To find the best cruise bargains, Fishkin advises booking early. Many cruise lines offer advanced booking programmes with lower prices. This is especially wise if travelling during holidays, summer vacations or school vacation periods.
Other cruise lines may offer discounts if you pay all at once, or come with a family or other large group.
Fishkin suggests asking if a particular cruise line has discounts for seniors, children, three or more people travelling together, or reduced or free airfare to the port.

Some other bargains might exist on repositioned cruises -- cruises whose itinerary has been changed due to weather or other considerations. Some repositioned cruises are deeply discounted with two-for-one prices.

Unfortunately for solo travelers, most cruise lines require a singler traveller to pay a supplement of 10 percent to 100 percent of the double occupancy fare. However, if the boat is not full, ask if the supplement can be waived or if there are rooms available on a "single share" basis, to share with someone of the same sex.

For men travelling alone, some cruise lines offer Gentleman Host programmes, designed to balance out the numbers of unescorted female travelers. These gentlemen are "carefully screened," Fishkin said, "and abide by a strict code of ethics." Discounts might apply in these cases.
Regardless of what you pay, a bargain is no bargain at all if it doesn't fit your needs, Fishkin said.

The first step in booking any successful cruise "is to determine what is most important to you. Cruising is not a well known consumer product. Ads or brochures alone don't help people get the right cruise," Fishkin said.

Look to someone with experience, Fishkin advises, such as a well-travelled friend or a travel agent who specialises in cruises. There are also books on the subject, offering up-to-date advice, including the Stern Guide, the Fromer Guide to Cruisisng and Total Traveller by Ship, written by Ethel Blum.
"Seek the advice of somebody with onboard knowledge of a particular ship," he said.

Your destination also will determine the type of trip and whether it's for you. For example, if you want to go snorkling or Scuba diving, your itinerary might include Cozumel or Grand Cayman. If shopping is your bag, a stop in St. Thomas is important.
To help book the right cruise, Fishkin advises asking yourself the following questions:
- What destinations are you primarily interested in?
- How much can you afford to spend?
- Do you want a party-like atmosphere or peace and quiet?
- Do you want to be with younger or older people?
- Is entertainment, food or service most important?
- Do you enjoy formal or informal dressing?
- Do you want guest lecturers?
- Do you need special facilities, such as wheelchair access?

The Cruise Line offers five free publications: World of Cruising Magazine; Guide to First Time Cruising; Guide to Family Cruising; Guide to Cruise Ship Weddings and Honeymoons; and Senior's Guide to Cruising. To order, call 1 800 777-0707.
